reading.body:
The clearest signal in this data is that frontier AI has moved from generating text to taking actions in the physical and digital world, with most entries here involving direct control of software, browsers, codebases, or physical bodies.

Six of the eight tools operate autonomously inside systems that were not designed with AI agents in mind. That creates a shared risk profile: credential exposure, unauthorized action chains, and safety-critical failures in environments where a human would normally hold accountability. The two robotics entries, Figure AI and Physical Intelligence, add a further dimension because errors propagate into the physical world and cannot be undone by rolling back a session. The notes flag governance standards for embodied AI as still emerging, which is a meaningful gap given that these systems are already in use.

The jurisdictional spread is narrow. Five vendors are US-based, one is Canadian, and one is French. Mistral's entry explicitly notes GDPR-first design and sovereign hosting, making it the only tool here positioned around a regulatory constraint rather than a capability claim. The data does not cover training compute, inference infrastructure, or energy draw for any of these systems, so no comparison on those dimensions is possible. What it does show is a category defined less by model size than by the degree of unsupervised authority each system is permitted to exercise.
